newsitem.title: USA: Court denies final effort to delay Oklahoma trial.
newsitem.headline: Court denies final effort to delay Oklahoma trial.

text.p: A federal appeals court on Friday cleared the way for the trial of Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh to begin on Monday as scheduled when it denied his remaining request to postpone it.
The court said McVeigh's attorneys were "premature" in asking for a delay on grounds of prejudicial pre-trial publicity.

"The proper occasion for determining whether prejudice is evident and cannot be avoided is during voir dire examination (questioning of proposed jurors)," the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 3-0. "We deny the petition as premature," the panel said.
Earlier in the day the appeals court denied two other efforts by McVeigh to have the trial postponed.
McVeigh is charged in the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City in which 168 people died.
The appeals court noted that the trial judge "has broad discretion in gauging the effects of allegedly prejudicial publicity and in taking responsive measures to insure a fair trial."
